text:
ada: Quick heads-up — I pushed a tiny PR to add a stacked-kernel fastpath when KV length < 64. Unit tests green but nightly microbench shows a ~6% reg at seq=1024.

mike: ugh okay. can you paste the bench command you used?

ada: ran the usual harness: `./tools/bench/attn_run --model=galen-1 --seq=1024 --batch=1 --iters=200 --config=stacked-fastpath`

sasha: do we see this in single-op microbench or only end-to-end?

ada: looks like end-to-end throughput drops, single-kernel latency is slightly better but we lose in batching efficiency. suspect scheduler interaction when mixing fastpath + fused ops.

li: can you drop a short perf log? the harness spits out p95 and perp-token times.

ada: pasted snippet:
```
ITER 200: mean_tok=0.0041s, p95_tok=0.0062s, throughput=145 tok/s
baseline: mean_tok=0.0038s, p95_tok=0.0059s, throughput=155 tok/s
```

jenna: thanks. @infra-bot can you kick a matrix of runs? need seq in {512,1024,2048}, batch={1,4}, and variants [master, stacked-fastpath, stacked-fastpath-no-fuse].

infra-bot: job queued: bench-matrix-2123456789 (seq:512,1024,2048) x (batch:1,4) x (variants:3). ETA ~45m. I'll post results here. :robot_face:

mike: meanwhile can we add a quick guard in the fastpath to only trigger when avg_kv_len < 48 to see if thresholding helps?

ada: yeah I can open a follow-up PR with threshold flag and an opt-in runtime flag `--prefer-fastpath`.

sasha: also add a debug nvprof trace for one run (seq=1024, batch=1) with symbol timestamps. we need to verify kernel overlap.

ada: will do. example command: `NVTX_ENABLED=1 ./tools/trace/collect.sh --run ./build/bin/attn --seq 1024 --iters 50`

li: heads-up for reviewer queue: @mike can you take a look at the PR when ada posts it? small diff but touch scheduler selection logic.

mike: yep I'll review tonight, leave a checklist in the PR for perf results and a small ablation.

jenna: if infra-bot results show the regression only at batch=4 we might have a batching bug. if it's across batches then revert and iterate.

infra-bot: bench-matrix-2123456789: partial results: seq=512 batch=1 -> stacked-fastpath +1.2% throughput; seq=1024 batch=1 -> -5.9%; seq=2048 batch=1 -> -0.3%. Full matrix returning soon.

ada: interesting — strong hit at 1024 only. I'll dig into scheduler logs around `prefetch_window` + `batch_collapser` for that run.

sasha: could be padding distribution that triggers different code paths. add a small script to dump token-length histogram per request in the harness.

ada: added `tools/bench/dump_len_hist.py` and re-ran locally — fetching hist now.

mike: once we have full infra results, let's decide: (A) tweak threshold, (B) gate behind flag for canary, (C) revert and rework fusion interaction. quick vote? :+1: A, :heart: B, :eyes: C

jenna: B seems safest for release window. we can ship opt-in and enable in canary stacks.

ada: agreed. I'll open the follow-up PR and tag @mike @sasha for review. updating thread with NVTX trace and infra-matrix when ready.

infra-bot: bench-matrix-2123456789: complete. attaching summary:
- seq=512 batch=4: stacked-fastpath +0.8%
- seq=1024 batch=4: stacked-fastpath -6.1%
- seq=2048 batch=4: stacked-fastpath -0.7%
- variant stacked-fastpath-no-fuse acts similar to stacked-fastpath at 1024 (slight -5.7%)

li: thanks infra. that pattern points to an interaction independent of op fusion, probably scheduling/kv-window edge.

sasha: next steps: ada traces -> nvprof + timeline, ada add threshold flag + opt-in, infra canary deploy to dedicated pool for realtime sanity.

ada: noted. I'll aim to have PR up in ~2h and paste traces here. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
